links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness of AI grading versus manual grading in DR telemedicine screening
links.effect: AI model ICER US $2553.39 per year without blindness; ICUR US $15,216.96 per QALY; AI not cost-effective versus manual grading (costs $3182.50 vs $3265.40).
links.quote: The ICER for the AI-assisted model was US $2553.39 per year without blindness, and the ICUR was US $15,216.96 per QALY, which indicated that AI-assisted model was not cost-effective.

unlisted_practices: Cost-effectiveness and cost-utility analysis of AI versus manual grading in screening programs
Sensitivity analysis of referral compliance effects on AI value

screen.reason: This study conducts cost-effectiveness and cost-utility decision-analytic Markov simulations comparing AI-based screening with manual grading using real-world retrospective data, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or operational practice.
